condition: recombinant WT B. linens encapsulin coexpressed/reconstituted with cognate DyP cargo in E. coli; DyP-loaded (DyP-E)
method: cryo-EM; native mass spectrometry; AFM; SEC; DLS; TEM
source: Snijder et al. 2016; Putri et al. 2017
notes: Biologically relevant cognate DyP-loaded WT T=1 assembly. Native mass spectrometry in Snijder et al. 2016 directly detected a 60-subunit encapsulin containing one hexameric DyP cargo (six DyP monomers; cargo:shell-protomer ratio 1:10). Putri et al. 2017 directly reconstructed DyP-E as an icosahedral T=1 shell and measured an outer diameter of 23.2 nm, compared with 22.8 nm for nonloaded encapsulin, corresponding to an ~2% cargo-associated size increase. The loaded and nonloaded maps had the same inner diameter, while the shell thickness was 2.8-3.0 nm; the internal volume of the B. linens encapsulin particle was reported as ~2.6 × 10^6 Å^3. DyP density formed a single hexameric cargo complex connected to the shell near one threefold axis through three ordered targeting-peptide contacts. Cargo loading lowered mechanical stability and was proposed to cause local distortion near a threefold axis while retaining the global T=1 icosahedral architecture. EMD-3612 is the icosahedrally symmetrized DyP-E map; EMD-3614 is the unsymmetrized DyP-E map and EMD-3613 is the C3-symmetrized DyP-E reconstruction. No PDB atomic model has been deposited specifically for the DyP-loaded B. linens state, so structure_id is left blank. DyP-E remained largely intact from pH 5 to 11 under the tested conditions, although aggregation increased at basic pH and partial disassembly was observed at pH 11; the smaller pH-induced species are not treated as separate assemblies because no stable discrete architecture was structurally characterized.
